title: Picking or retyping a caption answers at once
goal: Clicking a caption on the timeline, or double-clicking it to retype a word, holds the window for a tenth to a fifth of a second, on a talk with ten captions as much as on one with two hundred. In Premiere picking a caption is instant, and fixing captions is picking them one after another.
notes: Found by a-long-captioned-recording-edits-without-freezin (2026-09-24). Reproduced with a walk: openSampleTalk, captionsWaitForThemselves, wait, captionsEditFirstInPlace (select + beginRenamingClip), key escape, action selectCanvas, captionsEditFirstInPlace again, each followed by wait with longestUnderMS 5000. Output on the 17 s Sample Talk (10 captions): 'captionsEditFirstInPlace | longest 122.1ms; clipBar bodies 3, editorBody bodies 2, inspectorPanel bodies 6, layerThumbnail bodies 10, layersList bodies 9, layersRow bodies 16' and on the second pick 'longest 186.3ms'; escape 57.9ms; selectCanvas 54.8ms. On the five minute Long Talk (openLongTalk): 127.5ms and 188.9ms, so it does not grow with the number of captions. sample(1) of the Write Again path (which also picks the first caption) put most of it in NSHostingView.layout / CA commit: the panel switching to the text layer's sections and the layers list opening the Captions group to show the row. Worth checking whether the Arrange/Text sections and the layers list can avoid rebuilding when the picked layer is a caption.
acceptance: Picking a caption leaves the main thread busy under 50ms in one pass (walk wait notes, longest pass)
Double-clicking a caption to retype it opens the words for typing with no pass over 50ms
A walk picks and opens a caption on the Sample Talk and fails when the longest pass exceeds the bound

log.note: triage 2026-09-25: moved up in p2. The user's own ask fix-a-caption-one-word-at-a-time-on-the-canvas-a (p1, first in the queue) is picking words one after another, so this lag is what they will feel next. If that task already brings word picks under 50 ms, check whether whole-caption picks came along and close this.

reproduced: repro walk (openSampleTalk, captionsWaitForThemselves, captionsEditFirstInPlace, escape, selectCanvas, ...) longest 110.4 / 110.8 / 133.2ms per pick+open. Split with a new captionsPickFirst action: the single click was 112-121ms, opening the words after it 29-64ms.

adversarial review: the goal's real flow is picking caption after caption (Premiere's caption track is instant) and a double click to retype. The mock asks nothing new; this is purely cost. Knock-outs (panel hidden, sections dropped one at a time, timeline hidden) on caption-to-caption picks: panel ~20ms (mostly the Text section), timeline ~15ms, the rest ~10ms (SwiftUI accessibility focus walk the harness's in-process reads switch on).

cause of the 110ms: canvas shows [Canvas, Time, Captions]; a caption asks for [Captions, Text, Properties, Arrange, Appearance, Effects, Layout, Time]; the arrival catch-up built all six new sections in ONE pass. Fix: PanelSectionArrival.next, one section per pass, top down (InspectorPanel.catchUp). Pick from canvas now 38-47ms.

also: CaptionStylePreview .equatable() (5 tile bodies per pick -> 0, counted), SelectionMenu Equatable + TextInspector menus read pickedIDs at call time and are .equatable(). Caption to caption now mostly 34-46ms, occasionally 51-58.
tried and reverted: memoizing a style tile's frame by TextContent never hits (previewText carries per-tick animation state).

left rough (not filed, would not clear the bar alone): ~30ms of any click in a video window is floor (Escape alone 30-50ms): timeline rows re-running for every selection change and SwiftUI's focus walk. The 500ms passes seen three times during knock-out batches (captionsEditFirstInPlace after 6 picks) did not reproduce in 4 clean runs + 3 stall-loop runs (edits 34-56ms); recorded here only.

walk guard is 80ms, not 50: the same presses read 30-40% slower on a busy Mac (a-long-captioned-recording-walk's reasoning) and caption-to-caption touches 51-58ms on a quiet one; 80 still fails the old 110-190ms freeze.

Picking a caption after the canvas went from 110-121ms to 38-47ms: the dock now brings a caption's six new sections in one per pass, top down (PanelSectionArrival.next, tested), instead of all in one pass. Style tiles and the Text section's Font/Size/Weight menus no longer rebuild on picks that change nothing they show. Caption to caption mostly 34-46ms (occasionally 51-58 on a quiet Mac); opening the words 30-48ms.
